esePattern.questionType: Fill in the blanks carrying 1 mark
Subjective carrying 6 marks (3 from each of 3 modules)

subjects.title: Computer Programming in C
subjects.prerequisites: Ability to develop logic / flow of simple problem

units.title: Basics of C
topics: History of C; advantages of structured programs
Files used in C: source, header, object, binary executable
Characteristics of C
Character set, tokens, constants, variables, keywords, data types
Operators: arithmetic, logical, assignment, relational, unary, binary, increment/decrement, conditional, ternary, bitwise, special, comma, sizeof, postfix, prefix
Operator precedence and associativity
Type conversion and typecasting
Formatted input and formatted output

units.title: Decision Control and Looping Statements
topics: if, if-else, else-if ladder, nested if-else
switch case and applications
Conditional and unconditional goto; drawbacks
Iterative statements: while, do-while, for
Entry-controlled vs exit-controlled loops
break and continue; nested loops and applications

units.title: Subscripted Variables / Arrays
topics: Advantages of subscripted variables; accessing array elements
Declaration and initialisation: one-dimensional, two-dimensional, multidimensional (idea only)
Character arrays and strings
String variables: declaration and initialisation
Standard string functions: strlen(), strcpy(), strcat(), strcmp()
Substring extraction from left, right and middle; character replacement; concatenation

units.title: User defined functions
topics: Defining functions; advantages in modular problem solving
Prototype declaration; function signature; parameter types
Scope and lifetime of variables; storage classes: auto, extern, static, register
Function call: call by value and call by reference; return values
Recursion and the memory stack; types of recursion; recursion vs iteration

units.title: Pointers in C
topics: Pointers vs memory variables; declaring and accessing pointers
Constant pointers and pointer to a constant; null pointers; generic pointers
Pointer arithmetic and expressions
Passing arguments to functions using pointers
Pointers and arrays; passing an array to a function; array name and pointer
Pointers and strings; array of pointers; function pointers; pointer to a pointer
Dynamic memory allocation: malloc(), calloc(), realloc(); free(); pointer to a structure

outcomes: Computationally formulate basic problems and write code to execute them
references: Programming in C — Reema Thareja, Oxford University Press
Computer Fundamentals and Programming in C — Anita Goel & Ajay Mittal, Pearson
Head First C — Griffiths, SPD
C: Concepts & Programming — Bhusry, Willy
Programming in C — E. Balagurusamy, TMH
Mastering C — Venugopal, TMH
C Programming: Test your skills — Kamthane Ashok, Pearson Education India

subjects.title: Scripting Languages (Python)

units.title: Introduction, Variables and Data Types
topics: History, features, setting up PATH, installation and working with Python
Basic syntax; understanding variables
Numeric data types: int, long int, float, complex/imaginary
String type and operations: literals, manipulation, comparison, Unicode literals
Type conversion; converting to strings; string formatting; string methods
Date and time
Other data types: tuples, lists (definition, slicing, split, join, manipulation, copying), dictionary, arrays
Operators: arithmetic, relational, assignment (simple and multiple, tuple packing/unpacking), logical, bitwise, membership, identity
Operator precedence; understanding coding blocks

units.title: Control Structures
topics: Conditional blocks: if, else, elif
for loops and iterations; while loops
Loop manipulation: continue, break, else, pass
Programming with conditional and loop blocks

units.title: Functions, Modules and Packages
topics: Organising code using functions; defining and calling functions
Pass by object reference; parameters; arbitrary arguments
Optional and named arguments; passing arguments from a tuple
Variable scope and binding: local, nonlocal, global, class scope
Grouping code with modules; importing own and external modules
Grouping modules into packages

units.title: File I/O, Text Processing, Regular Expressions
topics: Keyboard input: raw_input and input; printing to the screen
File modes and permissions
Read functions: read(), readline(), readlines()
Write functions: write(), writelines()
Other file operations: open(), close(), tell(), seek(), flush(), fileno(), isatty(), next()
Redirecting output streams to files
Pattern matching: re.match(), re.search(), re.findall(), re.finditer()
Regular expression objects: import re, re.compile(), re.sub(), re.subn(), re.split()

units.title: Frameworks
topics: MVC framework; what Django is and why use it
Creating URLs and templates
Sending data to a template; displaying data and object lists
Filter chains; effective URL use; base templates and extension
Inserting static files into templates
Django forms: HTML form, handling submitted data, Django forms
Validating and manipulating form data; model forms; custom error messages and widgets

outcomes: Build programs with a scripting language and learn other scripting languages independently
Design real-life situational problems and apply Python features to solve them
references: Taming Python by Programming — Jeeva Jose, Khanna Publishing House
Core Python Programming — Dr. R. Nageswara Rao, Dreamtech Press
Python Programming: Using Problem Solving Approach — Reema Thareja, Oxford University Press
Core Python Programming — Wesley J. Chun, Pearson
Python for Programming — P. Deitel, H. Deitel, Pearson
Starting Out with Python — Tony Gaddis, Pearson
Introduction to Computation and Programming Using Python — John V. Guttag, MIT Press
An Introduction to Python — G. van Rossum, SPD
Practical Programming: An Introduction to Computer Science using Python 3 — Paul Gries, The Pragmatic Bookshelf

subjects.title: Data Structures

units.title: Introduction to Data Structures
topics: Basic terminology
Classification of data structures
Operations on data structures

units.title: Linear Data Structures
topics: Stacks: introduction, array representation, operations
Applications of stacks: infix-to-postfix transformation, evaluating postfix expressions
Queues: introduction, array representation, operations
Types of queues: de-queue, circular queue
Applications of queues: round-robin algorithm
Recursion: GCD, Tower of Hanoi

units.title: Linked Lists
topics: Singly linked list: memory representation, insertion and deletion at first, in-between and end
Circular singly linked list operations
Doubly linked list operations
Circular doubly linked list operations
Linked list representation of stack and queue operations

units.title: Non-Linear Data Structures
topics: Trees: basic terminology; binary tree concepts
Representation of binary trees using arrays and linked lists
Binary tree operations: insertion, deletion, traversals, types of binary trees
B-tree; AVL tree
Graphs: terminology; representation by set, linked list and matrix
Graph traversals: BFS and DFS

outcomes: Formulate basic problems and implement data structures and their applications
references: Introduction to Data Structures in C — Kamthane, Pearson
Data Structures Using C — Reema Thareja, Oxford University Press India
Data Structures — Lipschutz Seymour, McGraw-Hill Education
A Simplified Approach to Data Structures — Pawan Goyal, SPD
Data Structures Using C — Tenenbaum, Pearson
Data Structures and Algorithms — Aho, Pearson

subjects.title: Computer System Organization
subjects.prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computer systems and digital gates

units.title: Structure of Computers; Register Transfer and Micro Operations
topics: Computer functional units; Von Neumann architecture; bus structures
Basic operational concepts
Data representation: fixed and floating point; error detecting codes
Register transfer; memory transfers
Arithmetic, logic and shift micro-operations; arithmetic logic shift unit

units.title: Micro Programmed Control; Computer Arithmetic; Pipelining
topics: Control memory; address sequencing; design of control unit
Addition and subtraction; multiplication and division algorithms
Floating-point arithmetic operations
Pipelining: arithmetic pipeline, instruction pipeline, RISC pipeline
Vector processing; array processors

units.title: Introduction to Microprocessor Architecture
topics: Instruction set; architecture design principles from a programmer's perspective
Intel 8086: block diagram, pin functions, register structure
Segmentation; interrupt mechanism
Addressing modes; instructions

units.title: Assembly Language Programming
topics: Simple programs; logical, branch and call instructions
Sorting; evaluation of arithmetic expressions; string manipulation
Assembler directives; procedures and macros

units.title: Memory and Digital Interfacing
topics: Addressing and address decoding
Interfacing RAM, ROM, EPROM
Programmable peripheral interface
Cache memory: mapping and hit ratio
Virtual memory: logical address, physical address, TLB

outcomes: Understand the functioning of a computer system and its subcomponents
Analyse performance bottlenecks and choose an appropriate computing device
references: Computer Organization — Hamacher, Vranesic, Zaky, McGraw-Hill
Computer Organization and Architecture — William Stallings, Pearson
Microprocessors Interface — Douglas V. Hall, Tata McGraw-Hill
Microprocessors and Microcontrollers — Senthil Kumar, Saravanan, Jeevananthan, Oxford
Computer System Architecture — M. Morris Mano, Pearson/PHI
The x86 Microprocessors: Architecture, Programming and Interfacing — Das, Pearson
Computer Organization Design and Architecture, 5e — Shiva, SPD/CRC Press
Advanced Microprocessors and Peripherals — A.K. Ray, K.M. Bhurchandi, Tata McGraw-Hill
Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface — Patterson and Hennessy

subjects.title: Algorithms

units.title: Fundamentals of Algorithms
topics: Definitions and characteristics of an algorithm; examples
Data abstraction; sets and multisets
Stacks and queues
Asymptotic notations: order (O), Omega, Theta, with examples
Time and space complexity; best, average and worst-case analysis
Programming models: divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming

units.title: Sorting
topics: The sorting problem
Bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort, shell sort
Merge sort, quicksort, heapsort
Best, average and worst-case time complexity of each sorting algorithm
Linear time sorting: count sort, bucket sort, radix sort

units.title: Searching
topics: Linear search and binary search algorithms
Best, average and worst-case complexity of linear and binary search
Binary search trees: algorithms, search time and space complexity
Balanced search trees: significance and advantage of height balancing
Insertion, deletion and search in balanced search tree types; comparative study
Hashing, hash tables, hash functions, collision and collision resolution
Symbol tables

units.title: Graphs and Graph Algorithms
topics: Graph definitions: directed and undirected graphs with examples
Paths, cycles, spanning trees; directed acyclic graphs
Topological sorting
Minimum spanning tree: Prim's algorithm, Kruskal's algorithm
Shortest paths: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall

outcomes: Understand time and space complexity of algorithms
Design basic sorting and searching algorithms
Apply graph, minimum spanning tree and shortest path algorithms
Implement sorting, searching, tree and graph algorithms in a modern language
Understand string sort and substring search
references: Algorithm Design — Jon Kleinberg, Eva Tardos, Pearson
Introduction to Algorithms — Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein, MIT Press
Design and Analysis of Algorithms — S. Sridhar, Oxford University Press
Fundamentals of Computer Algorithms — Horowitz, Sahani, Rajasekaran, Galgotia
Introduction to the Design and Analysis of Algorithms — Anany Levitin, Pearson
Algorithms in a Nutshell — G.T. Heineman, SPD
Design & Analysis of Algorithms — Gajendra Sharma, Khanna Publishing House

labs.title: Computer Programming Lab in C
practicalAreas: Familiarisation with the programming environment (editor, compiler)
Formatted input and output (number formats, justification, specifiers)
Loop programs (GCD, LCM, series, patterns, primes, Armstrong numbers)
Arrays and strings (search, sort, matrices, vowels, standard string functions, palindrome)
Functions and parameter passing (nCr, series, factorial, call by value/reference, recursion)
Pointers and dynamic memory allocation (arrays, strings, structures, linked list, stack, queue)

labs.title: Data Structures Lab
practicalAreas: Stacks: push/pop, infix to postfix, postfix evaluation
Recursive programs: factorial, Fibonacci, Ackermann, Tower of Hanoi
Queue operations; recursion converted to iteration
Linked lists: singly, doubly, circular; merge and reverse
Trees: creation, traversals, deletion, binary search tree

internship.title: Summer Internship-I
internship.note: Inter/intra-institutional training, simulation programmes in institutes/technical colleges, or another department of the same polytechnic.

coverageNotes: CST205 and CST209 each declare four units. Any record tagged Unit 5 in those subjects is outside the published syllabus.
CST201 module order is Unit 3 = Arrays, Unit 4 = Functions. Unit titles in content must match this order.
The ESE pattern (page 14) totals 60 marks with 1/2/6-mark items across three modules; the paper data in this repository records different full marks — reconcile before any mock-paper feature.
The syllabus lists three labs (CST211/CST213/CST215) and SI201; this repository currently ships theory content only.
